source_text: Ἐγὼ δὲ καὶ τοῖς γεγαμηκόσι παραινέσαιμι ἂν οἴκοι τὰς γυναῖκας τὰς σφῶν μήποτε κατὰ πρόσωπον οἰκετῶν φιλεῖν. οὐδὲ γὰρ προσγελᾶν δούλοις Ἀριστοτέλης εἴα ποτέ, πολλοῦ γε καὶ δεῖ κατ᾿ ὄψιν αὐτῶν φιλοφρονούμενον φαίνεσθαι τὴν γυναῖκα. ἄμεινον δὲ οἴκοθεν ἀρξαμένους ἀπὸ τοῦ γάμου τὴν σεμνότητα ἐπιδείκνυσθαι. μεγίστη γὰρ ἡ σωφροσύνης συζυγία καθαρᾶς ἡδονῆς ἀποπνέουσα. πάνυ γοῦν θαυμασίως ἡ τραγῳδία. φεῦ φεῦ, γυναῖκες, (φησίν) ὡς ἐν ἀνθρώποις ἄρα οὐ χρυσός, οὐ τυραννίς, οὐ πλούτου χλιδὴ τοσοῦτον εἶχε διαφόρους τὰς ἡδονὰς ὡς ἀνδρὸς ἐσθλοῦ καὶ γυναικὸς εὐσεβοῦς γνώμη δικαία καὶ φρονοῦσα τἄνδικα. ταῦτα τῆς δικαιοσύνης τὰ παραγγέλματα καὶ παρὰ τοῖς τὴν κοσμικὴν μετιοῦσι σοφίαν ἐκφωνηθέντα οὐ παραιτητέον. ἐγνωκότες οὖν »τὸ ἑκάστου ἔργον, ἐν φόβῳ τὸν τῆς παροικίας ὑμῶν χρόνον ἀναστράφητε, εἰδότες ὅτι οὐ φθαρτοῖς, ἀργυρίῳ ἢ χρυσίῳ, ἐλυτρώθημεν ἐκ τῆς ματαίας ἡμῶν ἀναστροφῆς πατροπαραδότου, ἀλλὰ τιμίῳ αἵματι ὡς ἀμνοῦ ἀμώμου καὶ ἀσπίλου Χριστοῦ.« »ἀρκετὸς οὖν ὁ παρεληλυθὼς χρόνος,« ὁ Πέτρος φησί, »τὸ βούλημα τῶν ἐθνῶν κατειργάσθαι, πεπορευμένους ἐν ἀσελγείαις, ἐπιθυμίαις, οἰνοφλυγίαις, κώμοις, πότοις καὶ ἀθεμίτοις εἰδωλολατρείαις.« ὅρον ἔχωμεν τὸν σταυρὸν τοῦ κυρίου, ᾧ περισταυρούμεθα καὶ περιθριγκούμεθα τῶν προτέρων ἁμαρτιῶν. ἀναγεννηθέντες τοίνυν προσηλωθῶμεν [ἐν] τῇ ἀληθείᾳ καὶ ἀνανήψωμέν τε καὶ ἁγιασθῶμεν, »ὅτι οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ κυρίου ἐπὶ δικαίους καὶ ὦτα αὐτοῦ εἰς δέησιν αὐτῶν, πρόσωπον δὲ κυρίου ἐπὶ ποιοῦντας κακά. καὶ τίς ὁ κακώσων ἡμᾶς, ἐὰν τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ ζηλωταὶ γενώμεθα;« ἡ δὲ ἀρίστη ἀγωγὴ εὐταξία ἐστίν, παντελὴς οὖσα εὐσχημοσύνη καὶ δύναμις τεταγμένη βεβαία, τῶν ἑξῆς ἀλλήλοις κειμένων ἐν ἔργῳ καλῶς ἀποδοτική, κατ᾿ ἀρετὴν ἀνυπέρβλητος. Ταῦτα, εἰ καὶ τραχύτερον προηνέχθην οἰκονομούμενος τῆς ἐπανορθώσεως τὴν σωτηρίαν, ἐμοὶ μὲν λελέχθων, φησὶν ὁ παιδαγωγός, ἐπειδὴ »ὁ ἐλέγχων μετὰ παρρησίας εἰρηνοποιεῖ,« ὑμεῖς δὲ εἰ μὲν ἀκούσεσθέ μου, σωθήσεσθε, εἰ δ᾿ οὐ προσέξετε τοῖς εἰρημένοις, οὔ μοι μέλει· μέλει δὲ ὅμως καὶ οὕτως· »τὴν γὰρ μετάνοιαν τοῦ ἁμαρτωλοῦ μᾶλλον ἢ τὸν θάνατον αἱρεῖται.« »ἢν δὲ εἰσακούσητέ μου, τὰ ἀγαθὰ τῆς γῆς φάγεσθε«, ὁ παιδαγωγὸς πάλιν λέγει, γῆς ἀγαθὰ τὰ ἀνθρώπεια ὀνομάζων καλά, τὸ κάλλος, τὸν πλοῦτον, τὴν ὑγίειαν καὶ τὴν ἰσχύν, τὴν τροφήν· ἀγαθὰ μὲν γὰρ ὄντως »ἃ οὔτε οὖς ἤκουσεν οὔτε ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἀνέβη ποτέ«, περὶ τὸν ὄντως ὄντα βασιλέα τὰ ὄντως ὄντα ἀγαθὰ ὄντα καὶ ἀναμένοντα ἡμᾶς· ἀγαθῶν γάρ ἐστι καὶ δοτὴρ καὶ φύλαξ· κατὰ μετουσίαν δὲ ἐκείνων τὰ τῇδε συνωνυμεῖ, παιδαγωγοῦντος ἐνθέως τοῦ λόγου τὴν ἀνθρώπων ἀσθένειαν ἀπὸ τῶν αἰσθητῶν ἐπὶ τὴν νόησιν.
pass_a_gloss: I would advise even those who are married to love their wives at home, not in the presence of servants. For Aristotle did not even allow slaves to be fondly smiled at, and it is much more necessary that the wife be seen as affectionate towards her husband. But it is better for those who have begun at home from marriage to show dignity. For the greatest marriage of chastity breathes pure pleasure. The tragedy says, 'Alas, alas, women,' that among humans neither gold nor tyranny nor wealth has as many different pleasures as the opinion of a good man and a pious woman, a just and manly thinking. These are the commands of righteousness, and they must not be rejected, even if they have been spoken by those who possess worldly wisdom. Therefore, knowing the work of each, let us conduct our time of sojourning in fear, knowing that we were not redeemed from our vain conversation, handed down from our fathers, with corruptible things, with silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ, the spotless and innocent lamb. Peter says, 'The past time is enough to have done the will of the Gentiles, having walked in lasciviousness, desires, wine-drinking, revelries, drinking parties, and lawless idolatries.' Let us have the cross of the Lord as our limit, by which we are crucified and surrounded by our former sins. Having been reborn, therefore, let us be devoted to the truth and let us be raised and sanctified, 'for the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous and his ears are for their prayer, and the face of the Lord is against those who do evil. And who will harm us if we become zealous for what is good?' The best guidance is orderliness, being complete modesty and established power, well-disposed in work, unbeatable in virtue, with the following things laid out in order. If I have spoken more roughly, managing the salvation of correction, the Pedagogue says, 'Since he who rebukes with frankness makes peace,' if you listen to me, you will be saved, but if you do not pay attention to what has been said, I do not care; yet I do care: 'For God prefers the repentance of the sinner rather than death.' 'If you listen to me,' the Pedagogue says again, 'you will eat the good things of the earth,' calling human goods 'good,' beauty, wealth, health, and strength, nourishment; for the things that 'neither ear has heard nor has arisen in the heart' are truly good, being around the truly existing King, and are waiting for us; for He is the giver and guardian of good things; but the things that are named similarly here are according to a change of usage, with the Word pedagogically guiding human weakness from the senses to the intellect.

pass_b_english: I would advise even those who are married to love their wives at home, not in the presence of servants. For Aristotle did not even allow slaves to be fondly smiled at, and it is much more necessary that the wife be seen as affectionate toward her husband. It is better for those who have begun at home from marriage to show dignity. The greatest marriage of chastity breathes pure pleasure. The tragedy says beautifully, "Alas, alas, women, for among humans neither gold, nor tyranny, nor the luster of wealth carries so many different pleasures as the judgment of a good man and a pious woman, a just and right-thinking mind." These are the commands of righteousness, and they must not be rejected, even though they were spoken by those who possess worldly wisdom. Therefore, knowing the work of each, let us conduct our time of sojourning in fear, knowing that we were not redeemed from our vain way of life, handed down from our fathers, with corruptible things, with silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ, the spotless and innocent lamb (1 Peter 1:18-19). Peter says, "The past time is enough to have done the will of the Gentiles, having walked in lasciviousness, desires, wine-drinking, revelries, drinking parties, and lawless idolatries." Let us have the cross of the Lord as our limit, by which we are crucified and surrounded by our former sins. Having been reborn, therefore, let us be devoted to the truth and let us be raised and sanctified, "for the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous and his ears are for their prayer, and the face of the Lord is against those who do evil. And who will harm us if we become zealous for what is good?" (1 Peter 3:12). The best guidance is orderliness, being complete modesty and established power, well-disposed in work, unbeatable in virtue, with the following things laid out in order. If I have spoken more roughly, managing the salvation of correction, the Pedagogue says, "Since he who rebukes with frankness makes peace," if you listen to me, you will be saved, but if you do not pay attention to what has been said, I do not care; yet I do care: "For God prefers the repentance of the sinner rather than death." "If you listen to me," the Pedagogue says again, "you will eat the good things of the earth," calling human goods 'good' — beauty, wealth, health, and strength, nourishment; for the things that "neither ear has heard nor has arisen in the heart" are truly good, being around the truly existing King, and are waiting for us; for He is the giver and guardian of good things; but the things that are named similarly here are according to a change of usage, with the Word pedagogically guiding human weakness from the senses to the intellect.
